card.band: 8h. Two formats with finder detection, Reed-Solomon over different fields and mode parsing; frontier does one well, rarely both. Weaker models do clean images only.

Band.why: No dated public evidence of agent performance on this work; Han Xin is obscure and its spec is not in the image, so the difficulty is plausible but unproven.

Build.why: A 2000+ line reference from paywalled specs plus a generator and validation is likely 4 to 8 days.

Fit.why: TypeScript on Node, CPU only, offline, well inside 8 cores and 16 GB.

Hor.why: Two symbologies with locate, RS, mode parsing and distortion handling form a long multi-day scope.

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 base; new code can ship under the same licence; standards text is not shipped.

Multi.why: Independent buckets per symbology and per distortion type give steady partial credit.

Nov.why: Three neighbours sit above the 0.15 cosine threshold (0.216 max), so novelty cannot score 5; none is shown to be a public task.

Real.why: Real Apache-2.0 repo at a released tag with 1746 test files; the Han Xin and MaxiCode standards are real but paywalled, so the reference rests on purchased specs.

Ref.why: No reference exists yet; it would be written from paywalled ISO text and is unmeasured.

Seal.why: Hidden images stay unseen, but the spec is paywalled and not in the image, and the grader depends on exact mode details; a different valid solution must still pass.

Surf.why: Generated hidden images with noise, rotation and blur variants per symbology give thousands of cases with a deterministic exact compare.

spike_plan.kill_if: zint cannot be installed or run offline for the generator, the Han Xin output is not deterministic, or the existing MaxiCode reader already decodes nearly all generated samples (leaving no MaxiCode bucket to grow).
spike_plan.pass_if: Baseline MaxiCode samples decode at a measurable rate, zint Han Xin output is deterministic across two runs, and the RS round trip with poly 355 works.
steps: Clone zxing-js at v0.23.0 in a networked throwaway container; npm ci; run the full test suite and record per-test results and wall time (smoke_build was not run, so this is the first offline-build check).
Run the existing MaxiCode tests and samples from the repo to get a baseline pass rate for src/core/maxicode, since the README says 'needs testing!'.
Install zint 2.16.0 in the container; generate about 20 Han Xin symbols across levels L1-L4 and modes (numeric, text, binary, Chinese) and about 20 MaxiCode symbols.

Add rotation, blur and noise variants with a small script; decode the clean Han Xin samples with no reader yet, to confirm the generated images are plausibly readable and deterministic (run the encoder twice and diff).
Implement only a quick GF(256) poly-355 Reed-Solomon round trip against the zxing-js GenericGF to confirm the field parameters.
Record the MaxiCode baseline and the Han Xin generator output; do not spend time on a full reader.

v1.summary: The seed's premise is partly wrong: zxing-js already ships a MaxiCode reader (src/core/maxicode, marked 'needs testing!'), so the task must be recast as MaxiCode hardening plus a new Han Xin reader, and the Han Xin part rests on paywalled ISO/IEC 20830 text. The idea is viable at tier 20 (not the stated 8 h) if the scope is cut to Han Xin with a MaxiCode bucket, with a 60-minute spike to test the zint generator, the existing MaxiCode baseline and the RS parameters before any reference is written.
